properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued May 30 at 6:35PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
Air temperatures will rise into 70s across the Tri-State area
Sunday. However, water temperatures in the ocean and the Long
Island Sound will remain in the 50s.

The cold water temperatures can quickly cause hypothermia and
physical incapacitation to anyone suddenly immersed in the water.
When the water temperature is below 60 degrees, the average
submerged person could lose dexterity within minutes and be unable
to accomplish simple tasks. Anyone going out on small boats, canoes
or kayaks should plan accordingly and use extreme caution to avoid
this threat.

Several things to consider...

* Always wear a life jacket.

* Dress for the water temperatures, not air temperatures. Wear cold
water protection, like a wetsuit or drysuit.

* Carry an Emergency Position Indication Radio Device.

* File a float plan with someone you trust.

* Check the latest marine weather forecast, including water
temperatures at www.weather.gov/okx/marine before you go out on
the waters.

Your ability to survive cold water immersion depends on your ability
to stay afloat and stay warm until help arrives.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued May 30 at 2:10PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Ozone.

WHERE...Teller, El Paso, Pueblo, and eastern Fremont Counties.
Locations include, but are not limited to Cripple Creek, Colorado
Springs, Canon City and Pueblo.

WHEN...200 PM Saturday May 30 to 800 PM Saturday May 30

IMPACTS...An intrusion of ozone from high in the atmosphere may
result in ozone concentrations reaching the Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups category within the advisory area Saturday
afternoon and evening. Ozone levels should gradually decrease
Saturday evening.

HEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: Increasing
likelihood of respiratory symptoms and breathing discomfort in
active children and adults and people with lung disease, such as
asthma. Active children and adults, and people with lung disease,
such as asthma, should reduce prolonged or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued May 30 at 2:08PM MDT until May 31 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
are possible over the North Remington McGhee, Elk, Robertson Draw,
and East Side burn areas.

* WHERE...Portions of Montana, including the following areas,
Absaroka/Beartooth Mountains, Red Lodge Foothills and Southern
Rosebud and north central Wyoming, including the following areas,
Northeast Bighorn Mountains and Sheridan Foothills.

* WHEN...Until midnight MDT tonight.

* IMPACTS...Periods of heavy rainfall with embedded thunderstorms are
expected over the North Remington McGhee, Elk, Robertson Draw, and
East Side burn areas this afternoon and evening. Residents in and
downstream of these burn areas should be prepared for potential
rapid runoff, flooding, and debris flows. Narrow drainages and
low-lying areas are especially prone to flooding. Be sure to stay
up to date with information from local authorities.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of heavy rainfall with embedded thunderstorms are
expected across the region. The North Remington burn area in
southern Rosebud County, Elk burn area along the eastern slopes
of the Bighorn Mountains, and the Robertson Draw and East Side
burn areas south of Red Lodge, could experience flash flooding
and debris flows. Stay alert!
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Continue to monitor the latest forecast and be prepared to take
action should a Flash Flood Warning be issued.

Where: West-Central Montana Counties: Missoula, Granite and Powell.

Timing: Saturday May 30 through Monday June 1, 2026

Total precipitation amounts of 0.5 to 2 inches with locally
higher amounts possible in higher terrain along the Divide.

river levels rising. Anticipate further rises in local
waterways, rockfall and mudslide potential in steep terrain,
as well as possible urban and low-land flooding.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 30 at 5:22AM EDT by NWS Gaylord MI
properties.description:

gusty winds will result in elevated fire danger conditions across
northern lower Michigan today. East winds between 5-10 mph will
gust to 15-20 mph at times through this afternoon. Relative
humidity values between 20-30 percent are expected across parts of
interior northern Michigan with the potential for localized
minimum relative humidity readings in the teens. These conditions
support the quick start and spread of wildfires, so be sure to
take the proper precautions to prevent fires from starting.
